## Walkthrough

The pull request fixes object mutation issues in CRD reconciliation logic across multiple controllers. In both `karpenter_controller.go` and `ec2_nodeclass_controller.go`, the reconciliation loops were updated to iterate over desired CRD pointers and perform deep copies of each desired CRD before passing them to `Create` or `CreateOrUpdate` operations. Additionally, the `CreateOrUpdate` mutator closure now explicitly assigns `crd.Spec = desired.Spec` to ensure the original spec definition is applied rather than any mutated state. A new concurrent access test was added to verify that the reconciliation logic correctly handles concurrent execution without corrupting shared global CRD objects.

</details>

🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
karpenter-operator/controllers/karpenter/karpenter_controller_test.go (1)
`322-351`: **Isolate seed CRD objects per goroutine to remove shared-pointer coupling.** At Line 350, each goroutine reuses the same `existingCRDs` object pointers. Deep-copying those objects inside each goroutine makes the test fully isolated and avoids incidental cross-goroutine mutation paths.
♻️ Suggested refactor ```diff for i := 0; i < concurrency; i++ { wg.Add(1) go func(index int) { defer wg.Done() + seedObjects := make([]client.Object, 0, len(existingCRDs)) + for _, obj := range existingCRDs { + seedObjects = append(seedObjects, obj.DeepCopyObject().(client.Object)) + } // Each goroutine gets its own fake client and reconciler to simulate // independent reconcile loops all sharing the same global CRD variables. guestClient := fake.NewClientBuilder().
